name: PSD of raw data
summary: Computes the power spectral density of raw MEG/EEG data with MNE-Python's Welch method, saving per-channel PSD tables for gradiometers, magnetometers and EEG and PSD plots.
description: Reads an MNE raw file and runs mne.time_frequency.psd_welch separately for each channel type present (grad, mag, eeg) between fmin and fmax, with configurable time window, FFT length, overlap, window and averaging. PSDs are stored in dB as TSV tables (channels x frequencies) and plotted with MNE and with a manual plot. Use it to inspect spectral content or as input to peak-frequency Apps.

outputs.description: PSD table (TSV, channels x frequencies, dB) for gradiometer channels.
PSD table (TSV, channels x frequencies, dB) for magnetometer channels.
PSD table (TSV, channels x frequencies, dB) for EEG channels.
PSD figures (PNG) produced with MNE and with a manual plot.

parameters.description:
The length of FFT used, must be >= n_per_seg. 
The segments will be zero-padded if n_fft > n_per_seg. If n_per_seg is None, n_fft must be <= number of time points in the data.

The number of points of overlap between segments. 
Will be adjusted to be <= n_per_seg.
Length of each Welch segment (windowed with a Hamming window). Defaults to None, which sets n_per_seg equal to n_fft
Windowing function to use. See scipy.signal.get_window().

Whether to omit bad segments from the data before fitting. If True (default), annotated segments whose description begins with 'bad' are omitted. If False, no rejection based on annotations is performed.

Channels to include. In lists, channel type strings (e.g., [meg, eeg]) will pick channels of those types, channel name strings (e.g., [MEG0111, MEG2623]) will pick the given channels. When you use a list, don't forget to use the square brackets. Can also be the string values “all” to pick all channels, or “data” to pick data channels. None will pick all data channels. Note that channels in info['bads'] will be included if their names are explicitly provided.

How to average the segments. 
- If 'mean (default), calculate the arithmetic mean. 
- If 'median', calculate the median, corrected for its bias relative to the mean. 
- If 'None', returns the unaggregated segments.

options.label: Median
options.description: corrected for its bias relative to the mean
